CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty with asthma during sports activity and concerns about mood.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a student who enjoys playing water polo but has been experiencing worsening asthma symptoms that are limiting athletic participation. Symptoms occur primarily during aerobic activity and sports, causing him to stop matches and sit on the sideline to catch his breath. Patient describes sensation of phlegm building up in throat, coughing, chest tightness, and wheezing, sometimes accompanied by lightheadedness. Currently uses albuterol inhaler (2 puffs) for symptom relief, which helps with the phlegm sensation but requires him to sit down and rest for approximately 15 minutes. Notes tremor/shakiness as a side effect of the inhaler. Asthma symptoms occur essentially every time he engages in aerobic exercise. No nighttime symptoms. Also experiences coughing when around smoke and actively avoids such environments. Patient has not previously taken daily asthma medications.

Regarding mood, patient reports feeling increasingly stressed, sad, and unmotivated, particularly since the start of this school year. Attributes stress to SAT preparation, AP classes, and general academic pressure. Reports lack of motivation, preferring to stay home rather than socialize with friends, and experiencing fatigue. Denies difficulty with focus or information retention; symptoms are primarily mood-related.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports seasonal allergies. Denies nighttime asthma symptoms or other systemic complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Asthma

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler (as needed)

ALLERGIES
Seasonal allergies noted

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
High school student. Involved in water polo. Currently studying for SATs and enrolled in AP classes. Lives with friends and family.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not documented
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, sounds good
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Eyes: Normal
Ears: Minimal fluid noted bilaterally; otherwise normal
Throat: Normal, no tonsillar enlargement
Abdomen: Bowel sounds normal; soft, non-tender; no masses palpated
Reflexes: Normal and intact bilaterally

RESULTS
Physical examination otherwise unremarkable.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Asthma, exercise-induced: Start montelukast (Singulair) daily. Patient to continue using albuterol inhaler as needed for acute symptoms. Counseled that tremor is an expected side effect of albuterol; recommend sitting down after use. Follow-up visit in 6 weeks to assess response to daily therapy; expect improvement within approximately one month.

2. Mood concerns/Stress: Likely related to academic pressures and school expectations. Refer patient to therapist for counseling. Will administer screening questionnaires. Follow-up in 2 weeks to monitor response and review screening results.
